comment: Every model the application can download. One place a reviewer can read the URL, the digest and the licence of each blob, and one diff that shows when any of them changes. Pinned with `dart run tool/pin_models.dart`; ModelStore refuses to install anything unpinned.

models.description: Page dewarping, image-output export. Kept in the manifest rather than deleted because 'we measured this and rejected it' is more useful than an absence.
models.notUsableReason: Measured 2026-09-09: this export returns a rectified image at the input resolution, so getting a full-resolution page means feeding a full-resolution tensor. At 3000x2250 that is 487 ms and 477 MB of peak RSS on a desktop CPU — an instant out-of-memory kill on a mid-range phone. Use uvdoc-grid instead, which does the same work in 173 ms and 127 MB and then remaps at any resolution.

models.description: Page dewarping, grid-output export of UVDoc (ETH Zurich, SIGGRAPH Asia 2023). Input is fixed at 1x3x720x496 RGB divided by 255; output is a 1x2x45x31 coordinate grid in [-1, 1]. The grid is upsampled and the full-resolution page is remapped through it, so quality does not depend on how much memory the network was given. Two files: the .onnx references the .data sidecar by name, so neither may be renamed.

Shadow removal, SD7K weights, 120 MB fp32. Kept in the manifest rather than deleted because 'we measured this and rejected it' is more useful to the next person than an absence. The quality question is not settled — only real photographs can settle it — but the cost question is, and it is decided.
models.notUsableReason: Measured 2026-09-09..12: disqualified on cost, before quality even enters the argument. 10,612 nodes; the output is an image the size of the input, so a full-resolution page needs a full-resolution tensor. On a desktop CPU with four threads: 0.79 MP costs 3,566 ms and 534 MB of peak RSS, and loading the session alone is 2,606 ms and 338 MB. The application processes 6.8 MP. Extrapolated, that is tens of seconds on a desktop and minutes on a phone. Quantisation does not close a gap that size. A low-resolution gain field makes it 5x cheaper and still leaves a 120 MB download for a stage that did not beat the classical baseline on either synthetic test.
models.licenseNote: Traced 2026-09-12, corrected by adversarial verification 2026-09-13. The chain is clean, and saying why matters because the first pass got part of it wrong. Upstream CXH-Research/DocShadow-SD7K carries plain MIT (c) 2023 Nick Chen — Xuhang Chen, co-first author — added in the initial commit on 2023-07-16, months before the weights were released on 2023-12-17, and never modified since. No non-commercial clause in the licence, README, release bodies or the paper. The SD7K dataset is ALSO declared MIT, by its publisher (Department of Computer and Information Science, University of Macau) on the OpenXLab listing the README designates as the download, so no training-data restriction is inherited. fabio-sim's MIT adds nothing over the weights: it covers his repository tree and the .onnx binaries are release assets outside it. One gap remains and is stated as one: the upstream release body is literally 'Pretrained weights of FSENet', so MIT reaching the weights is an inference from the repo-wide licence rather than a quoted grant.

models.description: PP-OCRv5 text detector. Downloaded and verified by mobile_ocr itself; listed here so the licence audit has one table to work from. Measured 2026-09-14: opset 14, IR 7, 664 nodes, input [N,3,H,W], output [N,1,H,W].
models.licenseNote: Audited 2026-09-14 by the method in docs/model-licence-audit.md. Upstream PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR is Apache-2.0 — 'Copyright (c) 2016 PaddlePaddle Authors. All Rights Reserved.' — added in the initial commit bc93c549f on 2020-05-08, before any PP-OCR weights existed, and touched twice since (2608df32a, b9da97bea) without either diff changing a term. Unlike DocShadow, this does not rest on inference: PaddlePaddle's own Hugging Face model card for PP-OCRv5_mobile_det declares 'license: apache-2.0' in its front matter, so the grant is attached to the weights themselves. The card discloses no restriction on commercial use or redistribution. ente-io/mobile_ocr, which serves the file, is MIT (c) 2025 Laurens Priem and contains no .onnx anywhere in its git tree — the binaries live on models.ente.io, outside the tree that licence governs, so it adds nothing either way. ONE THING DOES NOT CLOSE, and it is step 4: PP-OCRv5's training data is undisclosed. The paper names a 44M-sample bootstrap set and a 22.6M-sample final set but identifies no corpus and no source. An undisclosed corpus is an unanswerable question, not a clean bill.

models.description: Orientation classifier, two classes. Measured 2026-09-14: opset 11, IR 6, 511 nodes, output [N,2] — a legacy-generation export, NOT the PP-OCRv5-era artefact this entry previously claimed. See licenseNote.
models.licenseNote: Audited 2026-09-14, and the audit contradicted this entry's own description, which used to read 'PP-OCRv5 orientation classifier'. Fingerprinting the artefact shows it is not from the same generation as det and rec: IR version 6 against 7, opset 11 against 14, graph named 'Model from PaddlePaddle.' against 'PaddlePaddle Graph in PIR mode', dimensions prefixed 'p2o.' (paddle2onnx's own namespace), 35 unfolded BatchNormalization layers where the other two have none, and a fluid-era output name 'softmax_0.tmp_0'. It emits 2 classes; PP-OCRv5's own orientation model is PP-LCNet-based and emits four. MEASURED: a Paddle export of an older generation with a two-class head. INFERRED, and left as inference: that it is the legacy ch_ppocr_mobile_v2.0_cls, which PaddleOCR still carries and reuses across versions. The licence answer is Apache-2.0 either way, since PaddleOCR's licence predates every model it has ever released — but unlike det and rec there is NO model card attaching a grant to these particular weights, so this one rests on the repo-wide inference, exactly the weaker footing DocShadow sits on. Closing it needs ch_ppocr_mobile_v2.0_cls_infer.tar exported through paddle2onnx and fingerprinted the same way, or an answer from Ente (U-14).

models.description: PP-OCRv5 recogniser. Measured 2026-09-14: opset 14, IR 7, 746 nodes, input [N,3,48,W], output [N,T,18385] — which is 18,383 dictionary entries plus the CTC blank plus the appended space token, so this model and ppocrv5-dict are a matched pair and neither works without the other.

models.description: PP-OCRv5 recognition dictionary, 18,383 entries. Not a model, but distributed from the same place under the same question, and rec.onnx is unusable without it: its 18,385 output classes are these entries plus the CTC blank plus the appended space. mobile_ocr's ModelManager.kt fetches it as a fourth required asset; this manifest did not list it until the 2026-09-14 audit noticed.
models.licenseNote: Same chain and same conclusion as ppocr-v5-rec, which it is paired with. Digest computed here on 2026-09-14 and matches the value mobile_ocr pins.
